title: Where to Eat Late at Night in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Most Berlin restaurant kitchens stop serving hot food by 22:00 to 23:00.** After that, real late food means a kebab counter, a späti snack, or one of a few round-the-clock spots, not a sit-down meal.

**Late food follows the U-Bahn hubs, not the guidebook streets.** The most reliable clusters are **Kottbusser Tor**, **Schlesisches Tor**, **Hermannplatz** and **Warschauer Straße**, all in Kreuzberg, Neukölln and Friedrichshain.
**The döner or falafel counter is the backbone of a Berlin night.** Cheap, everywhere near the clubs, and often open into the early hours.
**Spätis are the snack-and-drink safety net Monday to Saturday.** On Sundays many legally cannot open, so Saturday night into Sunday gets leaner before dawn.
**Central Alexanderplatz, City West and Hauptbahnhof are thinner late.** For the real late crowd, ride a few stops toward Kreuzberg or Neukölln.
**Getting home:** on Friday and Saturday the U-Bahn and S-Bahn run all night. From Sunday to Thursday they stop around 00:30 to 01:30, then night buses (the N lines) and trams take over.
